driver_scores.evidence_basis: JSS was a direct government wage-support intervention designed to reduce employer labour cost pressure and support job retention during the COVID-19 downturn.
The policy response was triggered by COVID-related economic weakness and demand collapse, making the broader shock an important contextual driver.
Circuit breaker and operational restrictions affected business activity, but the replay case is primarily about policy support rather than operational disruption itself.

final_attribution.summary: SG-JOBS-SUPPORT-SCHEME-2020 is classified as a policy-native replay case. The primary attribution is MKT_006 because the Jobs Support Scheme was a direct government intervention intended to stabilize employment and business continuity during the COVID-19 shock.

mechanism_summary.dominant_mechanism: Policy support reduced labour cost pressure and supported employment retention.
supporting_mechanisms: COVID-19 created demand and revenue stress for firms
government wage subsidies reduced employer cost pressure
automatic CPF-linked payouts reduced delivery friction
employment and wage outcomes were partly stabilized
